punchline: In Libet's experiment a brain signal showed up roughly 350 milliseconds before people said they wanted to move.
thirty_sec: Libet had volunteers flex a wrist whenever they felt like it and note the urge on a clock. The brain signal began about 550 milliseconds before the move and the reported urge about 200 milliseconds before. Harari uses experiments like this against free will, while Libet kept a veto for the last moment. Later work questions the reading.
